content: Recent environmental research has highlighted the significant impact of mining-induced deforestation across sub-Saharan Africa, utilizing large datasets to quantify the land footprint of mining concessions [64] . Many of these closures occurred without the allocation of mandatory rehabilitation funds, signaling persistent regulatory and record-keeping issues throughout the years leading up to the queried period [58] . These systemic failures likely influenced the databases responsible for recording mine closures, land rehabilitation efforts, and environmental impacts, demonstrating the urgent need for comprehensive historical data tracking to prevent future ecological liabilities [58] . As the South African mining sector navigates this transitional phase, industry stakeholders are increasingly focusing on collaborative platforms to shape future frameworks. Networking events and industry conferences, such as the Mining Indaba, serve as critical venues for discussing the future trajectory of the sector, even if they do not provide direct historical database access [61] . These platforms facilitate dialogue among policymakers, investors, and operational leaders regarding the implementation of the new digital registries and the establishment of more rigorous environmental and valuation standards for 2026 and beyond [61] . Features of Public Databases Tracking Mining Land Transfers and Valuations in South Africa Key Feature Description and Role Transparency Ensures transparency in tracking mining land transfers across South Africa Valuation Support Supports accurate valuations of mining land using public database insights Historical Data Offers historical transfer data to inform and guide industry decisions Data Source: Google Search Key Risks for Mining Land Held as Property Assets The management of mining land as property assets in South Africa presents a complex array of challenges, heavily influenced by a confluence of environmental, regulatory, and market-driven risks. As of mid-2026, the South African mining sector continues to grapple with substantial land-related risks that complicate asset management strategies and threaten the long-term viability of property investments. The primary risk categories impacting asset management strategies include environmental liabilities, regulatory compliance costs, and market fluctuations, each of which demands rigorous oversight and strategic mitigation efforts.
